text:
Alex: FYI — seeing a spike of GPU firmware watchdog resets in us-west-2, ~12 nodes rebooting in the past 18m. Root cause looks like recent firmware/driver combo. Starting emergency drain on affected nodes now.

Priya: oncall acknowledged. Can you post node list and impact on capacity?

Alex: node list attached below. Affected nodes are gpu-w-*-03..14. Priority: prevent noisy reboots from tripping autoscaler. Impact: approx 22% reduction on us-west GPU capacity, some jobs OOM/restart.

Alex: logs from one node: ```
[  124.513210] NVRM: GPU at 0000:65:00.0: GPU watchdog: GPU hung
[  124.513212] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65): 79, PID=0, GPU has fallen off the bus
[  124.513214] kernel: nv_watchdog: watchdog triggered, resetting device
```

SRE-Alice: thanks. Do not evacuate those nodes immediately if there are long-running stateful workloads — prefer cordon + live-migrate where possible. I'll run a quick health-check script.

Leo: I'm going to flip routing to pull 60% of inference traffic from us-west-2 to eu-west-1 and 20% to dedicated-us for heavy loads. Leaving 20% to remain so quick fallbacks work. Patch to routing config: ```yaml
route: inference-us-west-2
policy:
  - target: eu-west-1
    weight: 60
  - target: dedicated-us
    weight: 20
  - target: local
    weight: 20
```
Applying now. Expect some increased tail latency for eu-west clients.

Jamie: heads-up — cross-region egress will add cost. We should estimate traffic delta before we hold shift long-term. Rough calc: ~4TB/hr across regions => ~$0.15/GB => ~600$/hr. Will brief finance if we hold >4h.

Priya: I'll update status page and message major customers in the 1st tier. Draft: "We’re experiencing degraded capacity in us-west-2 affecting inference latency for some customers. Traffic shifted to eu-west-1. We’re actively draining and replacing affected GPUs." Thoughts?

Alex: looks good. Add ETA for hardware replacement: ordering RMA for 10 cards, ETA 48-72h but we can provision spares from dedicated pool in 2-4h.

SRE-Alice: running `gpu-health-check` now. If failures >15% of a node's GPUs, mark node for replacement. For now: cordon -> migrate pods with `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` on nodes showing repeated nv_watchdog.

Priya: oncall-bot: create incident and assign to infra-sre, severity P1.

oncall-bot: Incident #INF-2026-044 created by Priya. Pager dispatched to infra-sre. Link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INF-2026-044

deploy-bot: Routing policy change deployed to infra-router v2.1.4 (sha: b7c3f9). No rollbacks.

Leo: monitoring alerts: latency up 12% in eu-west-1, error rates steady. Keep an eye on KV cache hit rate — cross-region cache misses will add cost.

Jamie: procurement update: approved one-time spares transfer from dedicated to hosted for 24h to cover. Finance ok with short-term egress spend if we keep shift <6h.

Alex: coordinating node replacements and firmware rollback plan. If new driver firmware is root cause, we'll hold on automatic driver rollout in us-west. Patch: pin driver to previous release on nodes not yet updated.

SRE-Alice: agreed. I'll apply pin via machine-config and schedule controlled reboots after drain.

Priya: I'll post an update to #status in 20m with current capacity and customer notice.

Alex: thanks all — will post final postmortem notes after we stabilize. :white_check_mark:
